# Image negative supplement

This reviewed supplement contains **36 agreed semantic mismatches**: 24 reused TRAIN source photos from the existing image-pretraining fixture, plus 12 original repo-native SVG cartoons. It adds no new independent photo sources. Every target meaning is from TRAIN; no validation/test image or meaning was used. The first caption draft for memes was rejected and preserved in the work audit; only the revised, unrelated-caption SVGs are included here.

`blind-manifest.json` omits labels and reasons. `manifest.json` carries label `0` for each exact image/meaning pair, `distractorKind` (`photo` or `meme`), per-pair visual reasons, source split, source URLs, and hashes. `independent-review.json` records the second blind review and confirms 0 fit, 36 wrong, 0 uncertain. The SVGs share `parentGroup: original-smiley-meme-template-v1`; the template does not count as 12 independent photos.

Photo binaries and contact sheets remain in `work/image-negative-supplement/` and are intentionally not tracked here. To fetch the 24 photos and verify their pinned source hashes, run `python3 tests/fixtures/image-negative-supplement/reproduce_photos.py` from the repository root. It stores them under `work/image-negative-supplement/photos/`. The manifest asset paths resolve relative to `work/image-negative-supplement/` for photos; the original repo-native SVGs are also copied under this fixture. The source candidates are the original COCO val2017 candidates cited in the existing cases file; their TRAIN eligibility comes from the existing source/target meaning split assignment.

`vectors.json.gz` contains the cached encoder image and paired target-prompt vectors for the 36 reviewed assets. Its source-manifest hash ties it to the exact labels/targets; `vectors.json.gz.sha256` checks the compressed artifact. Regenerate it with `node tests/fixtures/image-negative-supplement/encode_vectors.mjs` after fetching photos. The encoder is the existing local MobileCLIP revision with FP16 text and FP32 vision; no downloads are enabled by the script.

This is reviewed training-eligible data only. It has **not been trained**; current CLIP and production behavior are unchanged, and personal preference/statistics data were neither used nor modified (`task: semantic`, `personalPreference: false`). Because it is negative-only, any training integration must combine it with positive examples.
